# labelmaker

A small template engine for the shipping labels and order mails of a web shop (Python 3, standard library only). Run the
tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Layout

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.

  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Escaped brackets

`\[[` renders a literal `[[` (the backslash disappears); other backslashes are literal.

# labelmaker

A small template engine for the shipping labels and order mails of a web shop (Python 3, standard library only). Run the
tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Layout

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.
* `tests/`: tests.

## Basics

* `Template(text)` parses a template (`TypeError` for anything but a string). A tag is `[[ name ]]`: two opening brackets, a
  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Listing the names a template uses

`template.names()` is the sorted list of the distinct names in the tags.

## Escaped brackets

`\[[` renders a literal `[[` (the backslash disappears); other backslashes are literal.

## Conditional blocks

`[[#if name]]...[[else]]...[[/if]]` renders by truthiness (missing counts as false); blocks nest; malformed blocks are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

- A tag can end in a chain of filters separated by `|`: `[[ name | trim | upper ]]`. Unknown filters, a missing or invalid argument, an argument for a filter without one, and an empty filter (`name |`) are a `TemplateError` at parse time. - Filters also apply to the fallback text.

As a web shop developer, I need conditional blocks in labelmaker. Templates need blocks that only appear when a value is set.

- `[[#if name]] ... [[else]] ... [[/if]]` renders the first part when the name is truthy and the second part (if there is one) otherwise. The name follows the rules of tag names (so dotted paths work when the template supports them). - `#if` blocks and loops nest freely, but must be closed in the right order: closing a block of the other kind is an error.
- Names used in conditions and in both branches of a block count.

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.
* `tests/`: tests.

## Basics

* `Template(text)` parses a template (`TypeError` for anything but a string). A tag is `[[ name ]]`: two opening brackets, a
  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Listing the names a template uses

`template.names()` is the sorted list of the distinct names in the tags.

## Rendering a batch

`template.render_many(rows)` renders once per item (dicts only) and returns the list of results.

## Escaped brackets

`\[[` renders a literal `[[` (the backslash disappears); other backslashes are literal.

## Dotted paths

`[[customer.address.city]]` and `[[items.0.sku]]` walk dicts and lists; a broken path is `MissingValue` with the full path.

## Filters

`[[ name | trim | upper ]]`: `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `trim`, `trunc:N` (cut with `…`) and `pad:N`. Unknown filters and bad arguments are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Fallback texts

`[[ nick or "friend" ]]` writes the fallback when the value is missing, `None` or empty.

## Conditional blocks

`[[#if name]]...[[else]]...[[/if]]` renders by truthiness (missing counts as false); blocks nest; malformed blocks are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Loops

`[[#each items]]...[[/each]]` renders the body per item (dict keys or `this`, `[[@index]]`, `[[@number]]`); missing lists raise `MissingValue`, non-lists a `TemplateError`.

  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.

## Conditional blocks

`[[#if name]]...[[else]]...[[/if]]` renders by truthiness (missing counts as false); blocks nest; malformed blocks are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

A small template engine for the shipping labels and order mails of a web shop (Python 3, standard library only). Run the
tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Layout

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.
* `tests/`: tests.

## Basics

* `Template(text)` parses a template (`TypeError` for anything but a string). A tag is `[[ name ]]`: two opening brackets, a
  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Rendering a batch

`template.render_many(rows)` renders once per item (dicts only) and returns the list of results.

## Dotted paths

`[[customer.address.city]]` and `[[items.0.sku]]` walk dicts and lists; a broken path is `MissingValue` with the full path.

## Fallback texts

`[[ nick or "friend" ]]` writes the fallback when the value is missing, `None` or empty.

## Conditional blocks

`[[#if name]]...[[else]]...[[/if]]` renders by truthiness (missing counts as false); blocks nest; malformed blocks are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Loops

`[[#each items]]...[[/each]]` renders the body per item (dict keys or `this`, `[[@index]]`, `[[@number]]`); missing lists raise `MissingValue`, non-lists a `TemplateError`.

# labelmaker

A small template engine for the shipping labels and order mails of a web shop (Python 3, standard library only). Run the
tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Layout

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.
* `tests/`: tests.

## Basics

* `Template(text)` parses a template (`TypeError` for anything but a string). A tag is `[[ name ]]`: two opening brackets, a
  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Listing the names a template uses

`template.names()` is the sorted list of the distinct names in the tags.

## Escaped brackets

`\[[` renders a literal `[[` (the backslash disappears); other backslashes are literal.

## Dotted paths

`[[customer.address.city]]` and `[[items.0.sku]]` walk dicts and lists; a broken path is `MissingValue` with the full path.

## Filters

`[[ name | trim | upper ]]`: `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `trim`, `trunc:N` (cut with `...`) and `pad:N`. Unknown filters and bad arguments are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Fallback texts

`[[ nick or "friend" ]]` writes the fallback when the value is missing, `None` or empty.

## Conditional blocks

`[[#if name]]...[[else]]...[[/if]]` renders by truthiness (missing counts as false); blocks nest; malformed blocks are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Loops

`[[#each items]]...[[/each]]` renders the body per item (dict keys or `this`, `[[@index]]`, `[[@number]]`); missing lists raise `MissingValue`, non-lists a `TemplateError`.

# labelmaker

A small template engine for the shipping labels and order mails of a web shop (Python 3, standard library only). Run the
tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Layout

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.
* `tests/`: tests.

## Basics

* `Template(text)` parses a template (`TypeError` for anything but a string). A tag is `[[ name ]]`: two opening brackets, a
  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Listing the names a template uses

`template.names()` is the sorted list of the distinct names in the tags.

## Escaped brackets

`\[[` renders a literal `[[` (the backslash disappears); other backslashes are literal.

## Dotted paths

`[[customer.address.city]]` and `[[items.0.sku]]` walk dicts and lists; a broken path is `MissingValue` with the full path.

## Filters

`[[ name | trim | upper ]]`: `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `trim`, `trunc:N` (cut with `…`) and `pad:N`. Unknown filters and bad arguments are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Fallback texts

`[[ nick or "friend" ]]` writes the fallback when the value is missing, `None` or empty.

        with self.assertRaises(MissingValue) as cm:
            render("[[#each order.nothing]]x[[/each]]", data)

# labelmaker

A small template engine for the shipping labels and order mails of a web shop (Python 3, standard library only). Run the
tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

## Layout

* `labelmaker/template.py`: `Template`, `TemplateError`, `MissingValue`.
* `tests/`: tests.

## Basics

* `Template(text)` parses a template (`TypeError` for anything but a string). A tag is `[[ name ]]`: two opening brackets, a
  name made of letters, digits and underscores that does not start with a digit, optional white space around it (including
  line breaks) and two closing brackets. Everything else is literal text and is copied unchanged. A tag with anything else in
  it (an empty tag, a bad name) and an opening `[[` without a closing `]]` are errors at parse time: `TemplateError`. A
  stray `]]` is literal text. `template.source` is the original text.
* `template.render(data)` fills the tags from the dict `data` (`TypeError` for anything else) and returns the text. A value
  is written with `str()`, except `None`, which is written as an empty string. A name that `data` does not have raises
  `MissingValue`. Templates can be rendered any number of times and `data` is never modified.
* `TemplateError` is an `Exception`; `MissingValue` is both a `TemplateError` and a `KeyError` and has the attribute `name`.

## Listing the names a template uses

`template.names()` is the sorted list of the distinct names in the tags.

## Rendering a batch

`template.render_many(rows)` renders once per item (dicts only) and returns the list of results.

## Dotted paths

`[[customer.address.city]]` and `[[items.0.sku]]` walk dicts and lists; a broken path is `MissingValue` with the full path.

## Conditional blocks

`[[#if name]]...[[else]]...[[/if]]` renders by truthiness (missing counts as false); blocks nest; malformed blocks are a `TemplateError` at parse time.

## Loops

`[[#each items]]...[[/each]]` renders the body per item (dict keys or `this`, `[[@index]]`, `[[@number]]`); missing lists raise `MissingValue`, non-lists a `TemplateError`.
